items.stem: Jade Ceramics keeps a petty cash book on the imprest system with a float of $200. During the week the petty cashier paid: postage $7.85, travel expenses $15.15, window cleaning $6.70, stationery $8.35, taxi fare $10.65. An accounts assistant said the petty cashier should be reimbursed $151.30. Explain why this is wrong and determine the correct reimbursement.
items.answer: The balance in hand was used instead of the amount spent; the imprest is restored by reimbursing what was spent. Correct reimbursement: $48.70.

items.stem: During the year ended 31 December, payments for rent by Aurora Printing totalled $17,380. You are told that $640 had been paid in advance at 1 January; $1,380 had been paid in advance for next year at 31 December. items.markingKey: (a) $7,800 − $1,490 + $570 + $360 − $290 = $6,950 [3] (b) Opening arrears Dr, advances Cr [1]; bank $7,800 Cr [1]; income to I&E Dr $6,950 [1]; closing balances c/d [1] [4]

items.stem: Tundra Outdoor calculated a draft profit of $38,200 for the year. It was then discovered that closing inventory had been overstated by $1,000, because some items were counted twice. (a) Calculate the corrected profit for the year. (b) State the effect of the error on next year's profit if it were not corrected. (c) State the effect of the error on the statement of financial position at the year end.
items.answer: (a) $37,200 (b) Next year's profit would be understated by $1,000. (c) Inventory (current assets) and capital overstated by $1,000.
items.markingKey: (a) closing inventory overstated → cost of sales understated [1]; $38,200 − $1,000 = $37,200 [1] [2] (b) Understated [1]; by $1,000 [1] [2] (c) Current assets and capital [1]; direction and amount [1] [2]

items.stem: Extracts from the records of Pinnacle Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2025: revenue $1,427,000; cost of sales $857,000; distribution costs $21,000; administrative expenses $37,000; 5% debentures $210,000 (interest for the full year is to be charged); tax on profit for the year $115,000. Equity at the start of the year: ordinary share capital $400,000, share premium $70,000, general reserve $30,000, retained earnings $87,000. Dividends paid during the year were $184,000. (a) Calculate the profit from operations. (b) Calculate the profit for the year. (c) Calculate total equity at the end of the year.

On 1 October Cedar Hardware had a bank balance of $2,470. During October: (i) Yusuf settled a debt of $1,400 by bank transfer, less 2.5% cash discount (ii) Noah paid a balance of $3,760 less 2.5% cash discount (iii) cash sales of $1,530 were paid directly into the bank (iv) Tomás was paid the $2,300 owed, less 2% cash discount, by bank transfer (v) wages of $700 were paid from the bank. (a) Calculate the amount received from Yusuf and the discount allowed. (b) Calculate the bank balance at 31 October, stating whether it is a balance or an overdraft. (c) Evaluate whether Cedar Hardware should increase the cash discount it offers from 2% to 5%.
items.answer: (a) Received $1,365; discount allowed $35 (b) $6,077 balance (debit) (c) Higher discount may speed up receipts and cut irrecoverable debts, but it reduces profit on every sale; the cost may exceed the benefit unless liquidity is a serious problem.
items.markingKey: (a) 2.5% × $1,400 = $35 [1]; received $1,365 [1] [2] (b) $2,470 + $1,365 + $3,666 + $1,530 − $2,254 − $700 [1]; = $6,077 [1]; debit balance [1] [3] (c) Benefit: faster cash/less bad debt [1]; cost: lower profit margin [1]; judgement linked to liquidity/cost of overdraft [1] [3]

items.stem: The following errors were found in the books of Lotus Retail: (i) A payment of $2,090 to the supplier Felix was not posted to Felix's account (ii) Office equipment costing $2,600 was debited to the purchases account. A suspense account was opened for the trial balance difference. Prepare the journal entries to correct these errors. Narratives are not required.
items.answer: (i) Dr Felix, Cr Suspense $2,090; (ii) Dr Office equipment, Cr Purchases $2,600
items.markingKey: (i) Dr Felix, Cr Suspense $2,090 [2]; (ii) Dr Office equipment, Cr Purchases $2,600 [2] [4]

items.stem: Lina owns Harbour Electrics. At the year end: inventory $12,600, trade receivables $14,700, bank $4,800, trade payables $10,900, accrued expenses $900. Revenue for the year was $159,000 and profit for the year $17,400. (a) Calculate the working capital and the current ratio (to two decimal places). (b) Calculate the profit margin. (c) Comment on the liquidity of the business.
items.answer: (a) $20,300; 2.72:1 (b) 10.9% (c) Current ratio is high – resources may be tied up in idle inventory or receivables.

items.stem: Ethan owns Orchid Pharmacy. At the year end the business had: cash in hand $500, bank overdraft $3,700, trade receivables $12,700, inventory $17,500, trade payables $14,700, premises $92,100, prepaid insurance $1,100, accrued wages $1,900, motor vehicles (carrying amount) $79,700. (a) Calculate the total of the current assets and the total of the current liabilities. (b) Calculate the working capital. (c) Calculate the owner's capital (net assets) at the year end.
items.answer: (a) Current assets $31,800; current liabilities $20,300 (b) $11,500 (c) $183,300
items.markingKey: (a) CA: Cash in hand, Trade receivables, Inventory, Prepaid insurance = $31,800 [1]; CL: Bank overdraft, Trade payables, Accrued wages = $20,300 [1] [2] (b) $31,800 − $20,300 = $11,500 [1] (c) NCA $171,800 + CA $31,800 − CL $20,300 = $183,300 [2]

items.stem: Harbour Electrics received $9,530 of interest receivable during the year ended 31 December. $1,520 had been received in advance at 1 January; $1,050 was owed to the business at 31 December. (a) Calculate the interest receivable to be credited to the income statement. (b) Prepare the interest receivable account for the year.
items.markingKey: (a) Received $9,530 + $1,520 + $1,050 = $12,100 [2] (b) Opening balance on correct side [1]; bank $9,530 [1]; transfer to IS $12,100 [1]; closing balance c/d [1] [4]

items.stem: The bookkeeper of Silk Route Textiles extracted a trial balance. The following errors were later found: (i) A payment of $2,720 received from Ravi was credited to the account of Daniel (ii) The sales account was overcast by $200 and the wages account was also overcast by $200 (iii) Cash sales of $3,560 were debited to the sales account and credited to the cash account. (a) For each error, state whether it would cause the trial balance totals to disagree. (b) Name the type of error in (i).
items.answer: (a) (i) no – totals still agree; (ii) no – totals still agree; (iii) no – totals still agree (b) Error of commission.
items.markingKey: (a) (i) agree [1]; (ii) agree [1]; (iii) agree [1] [3] (b) Error of commission [1]

items.stem: The following information relates to the sales ledger of Atlas Engineering for the year ended 31 March: balance at 1 April $14,220; credit sales $57,380; cash and cheques received from customers $47,620; discounts allowed $470; sales returns $3,930; irrecoverable debts written off $340; dishonoured cheques $1,370; contra entries with the purchases ledger $650; cash sales $7,640. (a) Prepare the sales ledger control account and find the closing balance. (b) State why the cash sales are not entered in the control account.
items.answer: (a) $19,960 debit (b) Cash sales create no trade receivable, so they do not appear in the sales ledger.
items.markingKey: (a) Debit: b/d, credit sales, dishonoured cheques [1]; credit: receipts, discounts, returns, irrecoverable debts, contra [1]; $14,220 + $57,380 + $1,370 − $47,620 − $470 − $3,930 − $340 − $650 = $19,960 [1]; balance c/d [1] [4] (b) No receivable [1]

items.stem: Volcano Spices: revenue $484,000; cost of sales $321,000; inventory $42,000 at the start and $72,000 at the end of the year; non-current assets (carrying amount) $605,000. (a) Calculate the rate of inventory turnover in times and in days. (b) Explain one reason why the inventory turnover might have fallen compared with last year.
items.answer: (a) 5.63 times; 64.8 days (b) Higher inventory held (bulk buying, slow-moving lines) or lower sales volume.
items.markingKey: (a) Average inventory $57,000 [1]; $321,000 ÷ $57,000 = 5.63 times [1]; 64.8 days [1] [3] (b) Valid reason [1]; explanation [1] [2]
